solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Extend jail sentence

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to lengthen or pull out further
second meaning: slang for a term served in prison

explanation.surface: A judge adds more time to a prisoner's term.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one instruction to lengthen a sentence; it is two separate meanings of one word, the second being slang for a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen something is to pull it out further, and a long spell inside prison is called this in criminal slang.

clue.text: Hang head in penitence after questionable outcome

indicators.note: after sends the penitence piece behind the questionable piece rather than in front

parts.note: informal clipping of suspect, meaning dubious

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the following word is kept

parts.note: opening letter of penitence
an end is a result or outcome

explanation.surface: A sinner bows their head in shame after a dubious result.
explanation.walkthrough: SUS is British slang for suspicious, short for suspect. 'Hang' looks like a noose; it is the verb to dangle.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang a thing is to dangle it from above, which is exactly what this verb describes for an object held aloft.

clue.text: Prone to mischief when caught in demo

indicators.note: the short pieces sit inside the word for a demonstration

parts.note: a rally is a protest demonstration
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Protesters arrested at a march are dismissed as troublemakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is easy to read as a link; here it supplies letters, as in 'as I left'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous rogue, so behaving like one means being given to impish tricks.

clue.text: Distended belly is delicate at first

parts.note: informal word for the stomach

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the two words before this phrase are wanted

parts.note: opening letters of is and delicate

explanation.surface: A swollen stomach is tender to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumid is a formal adjective for swollen or bloated, the same condition as being distended.

clue.text: Daring novelist caught violent criminal

indicators.note: to have caught something said is to have heard it, so the novelist's name is taken by ear

parts.note: Thomas Hardy, the Wessex novelist
short for hoodlum, a violent gangster

explanation.surface: A bold writer arrested a dangerous thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' looks like the cricket C, but here it means heard: HARDI is the novelist's name as said, not as spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardihood is boldness or audacity, a noun for the quality of a daring person; daring as a noun means the same.

clue.text: Artwork that is acquired by school body

indicators.note: what is acquired is taken in, so these letters end up held within the body

parts.note: Parent-Teacher Association
i.e., Latin id est

explanation.surface: A parents' committee buys a painting for the school.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ, Michelangelo's being famous.

clue.text: Luxurious as well as extremely homely

parts.note: plus means in addition to

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its outermost letters count

parts.note: first and last letters of homely

explanation.surface: A house described as both opulent and very cosy.
explanation.definitionFit: Plushy is an informal adjective for rich, plush and expensively comfortable, which is luxurious.

clue.text: A frost over borders of temperate Muslim land

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upward, so the phrase before it is read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
rime is hoar frost

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edge letters, the first and last

parts.note: first and last letters of temperate

explanation.surface: Frost settles over the edges of a mild country in the Islamic world.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a state ruled by an emir, such as those of the Gulf, so a Muslim territory.

clue.text: Radical associate on Left

parts.note: an ally is a partner or associate
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A political firebrand aligns with the Left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical' looks political, but it is the chemist's radical: a group of atoms that acts as a unit. In a down clue 'on' puts ALLY above L.
explanation.definitionFit: Allyl is a chemical group of three carbons and five hydrogens, and chemists call such bonded groups radicals.

clue.text: Lebanon wrongly imprisoning married peer

indicators.note: to imprison is to hold inside, so the rearranged letters wrap around the next piece
something put wrongly is out of its proper order, so the country's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
M is the standard abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: Lebanon unjustly jails a married member of the aristocracy.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a member of the British nobility, such as a duke or earl, so a titled aristocrat.

clue.text: Watering hole in Stoke, essentially unchanged

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letter is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of Stoke
as is: in its current state, unaltered

explanation.surface: A favourite pub in Stoke-on-Trent has basically stayed the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watering hole' looks like slang for a pub, but here it is literal: a desert spring.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile desert spot with a water source, where travellers and animals stop to drink.

clue.text: Temperamental wild sheep following German car

indicators.note: following puts the sheep second, behind the car rather than before it

parts.note: short for Mercedes
the urial is a wild sheep of Central Asia

explanation.surface: An unpredictable wild animal runs after a German car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' is part of the description of the sheep, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercurial describes someone of volatile, rapidly changing moods, which is what temperamental means.

clue.text: Attract fish back downwind

indicators.note: going back means the letters run from the end to the start

parts.note: to draw a crowd is to attract it
a common crossword fish

explanation.surface: An angler lures fish by casting with the wind behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeward is the side or direction sheltered from the wind, the way the wind blows, so downwind.

clue.text: Abraham's son prepared his meal

indicators.note: a prepared dish has been made from raw ingredients, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Abraham's boy cooked dinner for him.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Ishmael is the first son of Abraham, born to Hagar, the handmaid of Sarah.

clue.text: Dim and lowbred, struggling to be popular

indicators.note: something struggling is thrashing about, so these letters are thrown out of their order

parts.note: letters of dim and lowbred; and is a joiner

explanation.surface: A dull, common person tries hard to win favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' only joins the two fodder words and supplies no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Middlebrow culture aims at mainstream taste, neither highbrow nor lowbrow, so it is broadly accessible to the mass audience.

clue.text: Bishop is in need of cap going round dangerous place

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to lack something is to need it

indicators.note: to go round is to turn about, so the word for a cap is read backwards

parts.note: a cap or lid is a top

explanation.surface: A bishop needs his mitre as he walks around a risky neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A black spot is a stretch of road or district known for accidents or trouble, so a hazardous location.

clue.text: Periodically knocked out by certain mysterious creature

indicators.note: letters dropped at regular intervals leave every other one standing

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A boxer is now and then floored by some strange beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti, or abominable snowman, is a legendary ape-like cryptid said to roam the Himalayas.

clue.text: Madness of silly remark about lass's behind

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the remark wraps around the letter

parts.note: an inanity is a foolish, empty comment

indicators.note: the behind of a word is its rear, so only its final letter is used

parts.note: final letter of lass's

explanation.surface: Calling a remark about a girl's bottom silly would be crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Insanity is mental derangement, the plain synonym for madness in both medical and loose senses.

clue.text: Short version of Layla is included in platinum record selection

indicators.note: a short version is clipped, so the song title loses its last letter
included in places the pieces inside the metal's symbol

parts.note: Pt is the chemical symbol for platinum
the song title with its last letter cut
taken as written

explanation.surface: A radio edit of Eric Clapton's Layla appears on a platinum-selling compilation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites thinking of platinum discs, but platinum is just the chemical symbol here.
explanation.definitionFit: A playlist is a chosen list of songs or tracks to be played, so a selection of recordings.

clue.text: Stud retires, losing face and reputation

indicators.note: to retire is to draw back, so the letters run backwards
the face is the front, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a he-man is a macho stud

explanation.surface: A champion stallion is put out to grass, losing his looks and his standing.
explanation.walkthrough: Stud here is a virile man, not a horse farm: HE-MAN drops its H and is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's name can mean their standing or repute, as in making a name for oneself.

clue.text: Swimmers in America, between sea and earth

indicators.note: between means flanked on both sides, so the country sits inside the other two pieces

parts.note: short for the Mediterranean
the United States of America
E is the electrical abbreviation for earth

explanation.surface: Swimmers in the USA, located somewhere between ocean and land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmers' suggests people; they are jellyfish. Medusae is the Latin plural of medusa.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusae are jellyfish in their free-swimming bell form, so drifting sea creatures that propel themselves through water.

clue.text: Defaces and cuts suitcases

indicators.note: a word that cuts another splits it open and sits in the gap

parts.note: a valise is a small suitcase
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone scratches and slashes luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' looks like a link word joining two verbs, but it supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To vandalise property is to damage it deliberately, which includes spoiling its surface by defacing it.

clue.text: Complex design containing minute part that's barely visible?

indicators.note: something complex is intricate and tangled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: letters to rearrange
M is the abbreviation for minute, added to the mix

explanation.surface: An intricate pattern holds a tiny detail you can scarcely see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' adds M to the letters of design before they are mixed. The question mark flags a definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgen is a tiny amount, so small a piece that one can hardly see it.

clue.text: Pleasing line for daughter in amusing drama

indicators.note: one letter for another means swapping it in where the other stood

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line
D is the abbreviation for daughter
a comedy is a funny play

explanation.surface: A delightful line given to the daughter in a funny play.
explanation.definitionFit: Comely means attractive or good-looking, pleasant to the eye, so pleasing in appearance.

clue.text: Metal pan for Spooner's marriage

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the pair are exchanged

parts.note: lead is a metal and a wok a Chinese pan; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A metal cooking pan offered as a wedding gift.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of LEAD WOK gives WED LOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedlock is the state of being married, an old-fashioned word for matrimony.

clue.text: Jam-makers regularly added new spread

parts.note: the Women's Institute, a British women's club famed for making jam

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals keeps every second one

parts.note: second and fourth letters of added
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Fruit preservers keep adding fresh spread to toast.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI (Women's Institute) is a British community organisation for women, famous for jam-making. 'spread' looks like a noun, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To widen is to make or become broader, and spread as a verb means to extend over a larger area.

clue.text: Hellishly dark, dirty place, vast, without end

indicators.note: lacking its end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a pigsty, a filthy place
giant means huge

explanation.surface: A huge, filthy, gloomy pit that seems infernal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stygian refers to the Styx, the river of the underworld in Greek myth, so infernally gloomy and black.

clue.text: Bad-tempered, doubtless short of energy

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: surely means without doubt
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone grumpy is no doubt just tired.
explanation.definitionFit: Surly means sullen, rude and unfriendly, a synonym for grumpy or bad-tempered.

clue.text: Illness from merest dip at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means being confused and adrift, so these letters are muddled

parts.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone falls sick after the briefest swim in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is a viral disease of dogs and other animals, and an old word for any ailment.

clue.text: Bar and pub briefly bugged

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an inn is a pub
something that got to you annoyed you

explanation.surface: A bar and a pub with listening devices hidden in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' wants to be the pub; it is a bar of gold. 'bugged' means annoyed, not wiretapped.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of cast metal, typically gold or silver, shaped as a bar.

clue.text: Originally called deputy vacuous and insecure

parts.note: née marks a woman's birth name

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the inside letters are removed and the outer pair stays

parts.note: first and last letters of deputy

explanation.surface: A deputy formerly known by another name is empty-headed and unsure of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' looks like a first-letter signal; with 'called' it means née, French for born.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy people crave reassurance and attention, which is how emotionally insecure people behave.

clue.text: Act audaciously, investing last of money in satellite

indicators.note: investing puts something into, so the letter goes inside the moon's name

parts.note: Triton is the largest moon of Neptune

indicators.note: only the final letter of the next word is wanted

parts.note: final letter of money

explanation.surface: Taking a bold gamble by putting the last of your cash into a satellite company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'satellite' suggests a business, but it is a moon. Try it on is British for chancing one's luck to see what one can get away with.
explanation.definitionFit: To try it on is to test someone's limits cheekily, an idiom for behaving with audacity.
